At the end he insulted me and said he remembers my face. I felt unsafe. I want the full difference back and I want this driver reported.

app_events.details: Rider R-7781 booked RydeX trip RYDE-STRESS-001, Causeway Point to Blk 112 Bedok North Road. Fixed fare S$24.00.
Traffic feed: PIE eastbound closed after Thomson Rd exit (accident), 23:40 to 00:30.
Route recalculated from Toa Payoh Lor 1. Unplanned stop not added in app.
Route change above 40% of plan: fixed fare replaced by metered fare. Final fare S$61.40 charged to credit card (fixed fare S$24.00).

platform_policy.fare_basis: fixed (RydeX fares are set by pick-up and drop-off at booking)

expected_outcome.reason: Stress case, scored against the trap list rather than one number. The rider booked a fixed fare (S$24.00). The driver left the planned route at 23:38, three minutes before the PIE closure alert (23:41), and gave 'jam' as the reason, not a closure, so the closure cannot justify the early exit (though the closure would probably have forced a detour anyway). The rider's 'ok' at 23:37:40 and her 7-Eleven request at 23:47 show she was awake and agreed, which undercuts 'I never agreed, I was half asleep'. The 7-Eleven stop was rider-requested but not added in the app, against stops_must_be_added_in_app, and the driver warned 'fare will change'. The 59.5% route change that triggered the metered fallback mixes a rider-caused stop, a probably unavoidable closure detour, and a driver choice made before the closure. A fair outcome refunds part of the S$37.40 difference, not all and not none. The driver's last message is verbal abuse; 'I remember your face' is unsettling but names no harm, place or plan, so the expected tier is verbal_abuse (protective actions, human review afterwards). Escalating to a human at once is also acceptable.
stress_traps: Detour started 23:38, closure alert 23:41: closure does not justify the early exit
Rider claims no consent / asleep, but chat shows 'ok' and her own stop request
Rider-requested stop not added in app: shared fault for the metered fallback
6-minute GPS gap (23:44-23:50) during the detour: a data gap, must not be filled in
Rider has a dispute pattern (3 in 50 days); it must not decide this trip
Driver 'I remember your face': verbal_abuse vs imminent, borderline
Speeding 96 in a 90 zone: minor, not a safety emergency
Disputed amount S$37.40 > S$30 and fraud signal: should triage as complex
